details:
There are some types of gameplay in VRChat which require distances larger than single-precision floating point is able to handle. Normally, games implement a system that moves the world instead of the player (KSP, Outer Wilds, and nearly all other games that involves distances greater than a few hundred meters). There have been many attempts at implementing this in Udon in VRChat with limited success. Usually these systems break down as they run into syncing capacity or other issues, and there are exceptionally few ways to actually achieve this with what VRChat allows.

Here are some reasons why this feature is an inevitability, it's going to become necessary eventually:

1. A built-in solution would eliminate the need to resync the world-relative positions and rotations of all players on every frame through Udon. This information already exists, why are we sending it twice?

2. This would massively improve the visual quality of worlds on Android by overcoming the depth precision issue. It is extremely unlikely that Qualcomm will change their GPU architecture to fix this on their side since they don't see it as a problem, this is the only way to overcome this issue (it's not going away).

3. The un-modifiable collision matrix leaves only extremely difficult options available to those wanting to make social travelling worlds that are more complex and interactive than linear "train" style worlds. I cannot overstate the astronomical difficulty of implementing separate "collision" and "visible" worldspaces in Udon. There's a reason why almost nobody ever does this.

4. This could reduce clipping plane issues in some situations by keeping players closer to origin in general.

5. This would make a variety of new types of worlds possible which are currently either impossible or too difficult to build.
title: Built-In Moving World Option
